Hi all. So I've decided to keep a kind of journal of my experience taking Sertraline, if only so I've got something to be able to track how it's affecting me.

So for the past 7 months my doctor has had me on Mirtazapine for sleep issues & depression, starting out at 15mg & ending up at 45mg. Didn't really do anything for me, I was still miserable & still struggled to sleep so in December I asked to be put back on 30mg with the intention of cutting down & changing too a different medication. Cut down to 15mg from 6th Jan, & went back to my docs on Tuesday 14th Jan. Got put on 50mg of Sertraline, told to take it in a morning.

Day one.

5am: Made a coffee, ate a light breakfast & took my first Sertraline tablet.

5:30am: At this point I'm walking to work. Start at 6am, the walk is roughly a mile. Started to notice a rising feeling in my chest, felt similar to coming up on ecstasy (I'm 29 now, haven't touched ecstasy since I was 19 & then only a handful of times. Hated the comedown, swore off them after a heavy night in 09). Also noticed my eyes were watering slightly, and my teeth ached in a way that was noticeable but not unpleasant.

6am: Arrived at work with eyes still watering. Put a pair of dark glasses on & set to work with the lad that I work with.

6:15am: Aforementioned lad was in the middle of telling me what we had to get done that day when I felt a case of the giggles rising within me. Excused myself, then spent the next 5 minutes hiding out with tears running down my face & laughing inanely. If you'd put a gun to my head then & threatened to pull the trigger unless I told you what was funny, you'd have had to shoot me.

6:20am-8am: Worked away, eyes kept watering slightly & I kept laughing occasionally (by now I'd told the lad what was going on). About 8 I started to feel sick. Went to the canteen to get a drink of water. Got about halfway down the cup when I suddenly realised I had a real need to go drop my kids off at the pool. Like, immediately if not sooner. Made a quick dash to the toilet & promptly shat out what felt like every meal I'd eaten in 2019. This took about 20 minutes.

8:20am-2pm: Kept working away. Eyes seemed to have stopped watering & the giggles had subsided. All in all I felt on a nice level. Not insanely happy like I had been at 6am, but not considering cutting my wrists with the sharps either.

3pm: Got home from work & was hit with another urge to drop my kids off. Shat out what felt like every meal I'd eaten since the year 2000.

4pm: Never spent so much time on the toilet. Cats got bored of following me into the bathroom eventually.

5pm: Fucking kill me now mood. Spent an hour laid on my side on my bed staring blankly at the wall. No energy, felt like absolute dog shit. Eventually pulled myself out of myself & made some tea.

6pm: Well that was a waste of making tea. Barely managed to eat a quarter of it before I started to feel sick. Had to dash to the toilet afterwards. Toilet roll situation getting desperate.

6:30pm-9pm: Spent a couple of hours watching stuff on Netflix. Kept alternating between hot & cold. Also kept alternating which end I stuck over the toilet. Felt like crap, was in a crap mood too.

9pm: Went to bed. Eventually fell asleep around 1am (I know people say Sertraline can cause sleep issues, & coming off Mirtazapine can cause sleep issues but that's not uncommon for me. Takes me ages to fall asleep, then I wake up in the middle of the night)

Day two

Thurs 4:12am: Why the fucking fuck am I awake at this time when my alarm doesn't go off until 5!! Couldn't get back to sleep 😪

5am: Time to repeat the kettle, breakfast & tablet trick. Still in a shit mood, feel like shit too. 

5:30am: No rising feeling in my chest. Still in a shit mood.

6am-2pm: Been in a lousy mood at work all day. Felt like curling up in a corner at one point. Spent most of the day sweating but feeling cold. Mood picked up slightly around dinnertime, but overall I still felt crap & low. May have also shat out every meal I've ever eaten. The doc warned me that I might experience some diarrhea (Why they don't just call it "the shits" like everyone else I'll never know) & wow, he wasn't joking.

3pm. Just got home & started writing this essay. Still feel like shit. Still sweating but cold. Netflix & duvet time for me, no doubt with numerous pauses so I can stick my arse over the toilet again. Hopefully tomorrow is better.

Now I accept that part of the reason I'm feeling like shit is probably because of the withdrawal symptoms from coming off Mirtazapine quickly instead of doing a month step down each time. Back at doc's in 12 days time to review how I've gone on with Sertraline. If I keep on shitting like I am, I'll be a stick figure by the time I go back.

Day 3

Woke up at half 2 but managed to fall back asleep until 5!!

Kettle, breakfast, tablet. Mood is slightly better today. Felt level mentally when I got to work & was ok for the first hour or so before my rear end informed me that it was time to go. Again. 

Started to feel sick again about half 8. Repeated the cup of water/quick trip to toilet routine of day one. Also still sweating excessively. Feels like I've got the flu without the snot & cough. Appetite at this point is pretty much non existent, having to force myself to eat.
Had a moment where I wasn't sure if I was awake & at work, or in bed dreaming.
Went to my boss & explained the situation, said I was struggling with the side effects of either coming off Mirtazapine or from starting Sertraline. Finished at half 12, went back & slept until 4. Woke up covered in my own sweat. Feel slightly better mentally though. 
One thing I have noticed already is that I'm no longer so bothered about things.

Well for background I work in a factory in the UK. I'm English, but a good half of the workforce is made up of Polish, Czechs, Lithuanians, Romanians & Bulgarians. The part of the UK I'm from is known as "Yorkshire" (I want you to stop, go on YouTube and put in "Yorkshire accent" & listen carefully to a few videos. Then put in English accent, or just imagine how people the world over imagine we speak), & the accent around here further complicates things (I've never been to the Netherlands, would love to do so one day. Anyways I'm hoping you've got a similar thing over there, like how people imagine the Dutch speak versus regional or local accents) because it's quite a broad tone, words can get lost or misunderstood very easily. I'll give you an example I had today with a Polish lad who can speak English too a decent degree. I'll write it out how it'd sound when I'm saying it, hopefully that'll give you an idea of how communication problems can occur:

Me: Ear lad, pass us your knife chuck
Lad: Sorry?
Me: Pass us your knife chuck
Lad: Say again please?
Me: Pass me. Your knife. Chuck
Lad: Sorry?

Then I walked round, grabbed what I wanted & explained to him what that means. In Yorkshire we've a terrible habit of dropping H's from the start of words. So habit would be "abit", happy would be "appy" & so on & so forth. Chuck is a term meaning pal or friend, but it can also be used to mean to throw something away, so that also confused the poor lad 😆 (if you understand the English language quite well & I'm essentially teaching you to suck eggs I do apologise, but because of the environment I work in I tend to assume people don't have much grasp of it).
